source_piece.title: That Viral Anthropic Chart Does Not Say What You Think It Does

hook.headline: Good news for people whose jobs are being reshaped by AI

platform_cuts.linkedin:
Indeed Hiring Lab: median advertised pay for the jobs most exposed to AI has grown 46% since 2021. Less-exposed jobs: 25%.

That tracks with how I read the AI exposure charts. I see them primarily as an opportunity gap map. The delta between what AI is actually doing in practice and what it could theoretically assist with represents the space to build tools that fill the gap.

That's a product roadmap, not a pink slip.

One caveat worth watching: the pay gap barely shows up for entry-level roles. It widens with seniority.

items.passage: Step three is ownership, and this is where most companies are flying blind. The organizations figuring this out have an AI lead who is AI-native, or close to it, overseeing usage across the company. When AI lives inside the legacy IT department, you get process and compliance. Experimentation and cost discipline come from giving it its own home.

source_piece.title: A French Magazine Quoted Me on AI Agents. Here's My Full Take on What the Real Cost of AI Means for Your Organization.

items.passage: Welcome to the world of AI theater, where companies — and increasingly, individuals — engage in performative, often exaggerated proclamations about artificial intelligence. These proclamations are rarely about the tech itself. More often, they’re veiled marketing schemes, brand-building exercises, or clever distractions.

source_piece.title: Stop Falling for Corporate AI Theater

items.passage: For now, I use it without any concern for cost, not just because it’s free but also because Instinct’s venture capital subsidizes my token usage and the computing I consume every time it’s working on my behalf. As I’ve written before, free and heavily subsidized tokens are going away. I keep asking myself how much I’d pay for this, and how I’d use it differently if every prompt, task, and project cost money.

items.passage: Consumption does not go hand in hand with productivity. There’s a lot of conflation between AI activity and AI productivity. People are doing lots of stuff with AI. The activity is real. How much of that activity is actually productive remains an open question.

source_piece.title: A French Magazine Quoted Me on AI Agents. Here's My Full Take on What the Real Cost of AI Means for Your Organization.

platform_cuts.linkedin:
Token consumption does not go hand in hand with productivity.

There’s a lot of conflation between AI activity and AI productivity. People are doing lots of stuff with AI. The activity is real. How much of that activity is actually productive remains an open question.

Finance should be asking that question before the budget line grows, not after.
